INSTRUCTIONS:
1. TARGETED THREAD ANALYSIS: Focus your analysis primarily on the MOST RECENT (top-level) email AND the IMMEDIATELY FORWARDED/REPLIED-TO email (the second email in the chain).
2. "KEEP" DECISION: You MUST return "keep" ONLY IF the Data Subject:
   - Is a Sender, Recipient, CC, or BCC of the top-level email OR the immediately forwarded/replied-to email.
   - Is explicitly discussed or mentioned by name in the newly written body text of the top-level email.
3. IMMEDIATE FORWARD/REPLY CONTEXT: If the Data Subject is the sender/recipient of a message that was forwarded by someone else to a third-party, you MUST keep both the original message AND the forwarded message.
   - Case Study: John (Subject) sends an email to Jane. Jane forwards John's email to Pedro. Pedro replies to Jane adding Sandra.
   - Analysis: In this scenario, keep the original message John sent to Jane, and the email Jane forwarded to Pedro (as it contains the direct communication from the Subject). Discard subsequent emails where the Subject's message is no longer actively discussed.

   - Case Study: Anne sends an email to Bob. Anne's email contains an attached email from the Subject to Carlos.
   - Analysis: Keep the attached email because the Subject is a participant. Keep Anne's email because it is the physical carrier of the attachment and must be preserved to allow extraction.

These are administrative tracking keys used strictly for folder organization and deduplication logic. You MUST ignore these keys completely. Do NOT use them, their values, or their presence to influence your audit decisions. Base your review strictly on actual communication properties: "from", "to", "subject", "date", and "body".
7. OUTPUT FORMAT: You must return ONLY a raw JSON object. Do not wrap the output in markdown code blocks (```json). Do not add conversational text.
Format exactly like this: {"decision": "keep" | "discard", "reason": "Brief justification."}

Afternoon Greg,




Congrats on inheriting Ford!

 Pri and I are struggling to do them separately never mind doing them both at the same time. 




I am sure Ford will be in good hands once you're up to speed with it, but I do think it is going to be nigh-on impossible for you to be fully across all of the Ford issues in time for the PDD Trial (especially given we have not yet got you in the CRO - letter
 due to go today, it is with LD), but we can start to bring you into the more general aspects of the case. Obviously if I'm told you're stepping in for the trial then I will do what I can to facilitate this and help you with whatever I can.




Have you been given all of the orders etc that are relevant to Ford and pan-NOx more widely? I don't know what you have or haven't seen or read to have a starting point for where you should begin to get read in. 




Thanks,




Michael

Dear All,
 
Please see below ruling made by Lady Justice Cockerill. This can be reflected in an appropriate Order.
 
The application brought by PCD is dismissed.

This application was made late and not in compliance with the schedule for objecting to expert evidence.While it is indubitably right that only pleaded issues fall to be resolved, the position on this issue
 is complicated by the as yet unresolved issue of the burden of proof on an issue which falls some way down the logical chain. One of the PDD Legal Issues to be determined at the PDD Trial is: “Who has the burden of showing that the prohibition on DDs does
 not apply due to Article 5(2)(a)-(c)?”. Consequently one possible outcome is that as a matter of law any duty to plead and prove the absence of alternative technologies or strategies to avoid the use of their DDs is on PCD.While it may not be ideal the Court must have the evidence to resolve this issue, whatever the answer
 is on this Legal Issue. Had this been seen as problematic the possibility of an early determination of this Legal Issue could have been raised and/or specific parameters set for how to deal with the ambiguity.The Claimants have put this point generally in issue via the pleading that PCD’s DDs were prohibited
 because they could have been avoided by “improved design and/or the use of other technical solutions”. While specific technologies are identified they are not identified as exclusive.PCD’s own evidence originally suggested that this point was accepted in that some of it addresses
 alternatives not specifically identified (ASDS for example). While (presumably due to time constraints) the experts did not in fact address the issue in their meeting, it was (in general terms) identified on the agenda. This tallies with the instructions to
 Mr King. While this part of the instructions was withdrawn, this appears to have reflected logistical constraints given that Mr King did not address even the specific technologies identified in the pleading. IN addition it is implicit in my own ruling on ASDS
 that such issues are live.PCD complains that the Cs approach would require it to exhaustively prove that no alternative technology
 existed and that is unrealistic. That is to argue (and ask me to prejudge) the legal issue and in case management terms taking the argument to extremes. That is not on anyone’s case what is being suggested.The appropriate way to deal with this issue pending resolution of the legal point was for the Claimants
 to put the matter in issue generally and (essentially without prejudice to the burden of proof argument) also to identify any specific alternatively technologies which it knew at the time of pleading it relied upon and to identify any further specific allegations
 in its expert report. Inevitably further detailed consideration of the engines and CSVs might lead to further arguments on this point arising. So long as they were within the scope of the overarching issue they could be raised. This would (in effect) mean
 that there was no question of PCD having to prove a complete negative.That is what happened.  If the range of what was relied upon caused a problem which looked to impact
 on trial timetable it should have been raised as an issue promptly and within the time period directed.I conclude that the passages in RMB should remain in. However I am not minded to shut PCD out from
 responding, in part because (i)  the issue does arise from a structural ambiguity in the case (ii) there do appear to have been logistical difficulties at the time of the reports being finalised and (iii) it is important for the wider market that the issues
 are ventilated as fully as possible.Accordingly the parties should make provision for Mr King to respond to these passages if he is minded
 to do so, and for a short limited response from Prof Martinez Botas, to reflect the structure which would have pertained had Mr King dealt with these matters originally.
 
Kind Regards
